stimulus.source_note: Table compiled from the National Center for Education Statistics, Digest of Education Statistics, Table 303.10.
stimulus.text:
Students enrolled in colleges and universities each fall (National Center for Education Statistics, Digest of Education Statistics, Table 303.10):

| Fall | Total enrollment | Women as a share of students |
| 1950 | 2.3 million | 31.6% |
| 1959 | 3.6 million | 35.9% |
| 1970 | 8.6 million | 41.2% |
| 1980 | 12.1 million | 51.4% |

stem: What does the table show about college enrollment from 1950 to 1980?

options.text: Enrollment grew about fivefold, and women went from under a third of students to over half.
Enrollment fell after 1970 as the baby boom ended and fewer young students applied.
options.misconception: The table rises from 8.6 million in 1970 to 12.1 million in 1980.

options.text: Women were already the majority of students in 1950, well before the boom years began.
options.misconception: The table gives women 31.6 percent of students in 1950.

options.text: Enrollment stayed below 5 million students through 1980 and never rose above that mark.
options.misconception: The table passes 5 million between 1959 and 1970 and reaches 12.1 million in 1980.

rationales.A: Total enrollment rises from 2.3 million to 12.1 million, and the women's share rises from 31.6 percent to 51.4 percent.
rationales.B: The table rises from 8.6 million in 1970 to 12.1 million in 1980.
rationales.C: The table gives women 31.6 percent of students in 1950.
rationales.D: The table passes 5 million between 1959 and 1970 and reaches 12.1 million in 1980.
rationales.general:
1. Read the total column first: 2.3, 3.6, 8.6, 12.1 million, rising at every step.
2. Twelve million is about five times 2.3 million.
3. Read the women's column the same way: 31.6, 35.9, 41.2, 51.4 percent, passing half only in 1980.
4. An answer must fit both columns, not just one.
Remember: A table with two columns asks for two readings, one per column.
